newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. debt volatilities narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. debt volatilities narrowly mixed.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. debt options were narrowly mixed in late trade as underlying markets erased their small early losses, dealers said.

Implied volatilities for CBOT January and March T-bond futures options stood at 9.3 and 9.9 percent respectively with about half an hour left to trade, off 0.1 point from Tuesday but up slightly from early lows.
"After the open things came off a little bit but, surprisingly, they got bid back up," said a Treasury bond trader at the Chicago Board of Trade.
Traders said growing expectations that T-bonds would extend recent rallies and rise back toward January highs prompted some big trades in deep out-of-the-money calls.
A brokerage firm was said to have bought 10,000 contracts of March 124 calls. A second firm was seen selling 5,000 lots of March 20 calls and an investment bank sold 5,000 of January 19 calls.

Still, volatilities were generally under pressure after the market digested the Treasury's two-year note offering Tuesday and five-year notes today without much trouble and with the Thanksgiving holiday coming up next week.

The five-year note auction produced a high yield of 5.950 percent and a bid-to-cover ratio of 2.86 times. Debt futures showed little reaction to the results initially but later started to drift upward.
"It came out pretty much where people had expected," said an investment bank trader at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange. "I think it's a little bit of a relief to have these auctions behind us."
Front-end Eurodollar volatilities were pressured because, in addition to the steep time decay, March and June futures were gravitating toward parity with cash rates.

"A lot of interest has moved further out the curve," the CME trader said. He said he saw some five-year bundles trading prior to the auction results but that the shorter end of the curve had been very quiet today.
Implied volatilities for CME March and June Eurodollar futures options were little changed from Tuesday at 10.4 and 14.6 percent respectively.
